author: Robert Carr
description: Skillet-seared all-beef hot dogs in butter-toasted potato buns with sharp cheddar, golden Worcestershire onions, crunchy jalapeno-pickle relish, and chipotle-lime mustard mayo. Gentle reheating followed by a brief sear keeps the focus on a juicy frank, with adjustable heat and contrasting textures.
equipment: 12-inch stainless steel or cast-iron skillet with a lid

Or another neutral high-heat cooking oil; divided between onions and franks.
One medium onion, about 6 to 8 oz before trimming.
Measure after draining and chopping; choose hot rather than mild for more heat.
Measure after draining and chopping; use crisp pickles, not sweet relish.
Use 1 small pepper (about 2 tsp minced) and 1 tsp sauce from the same can. Quantity is one pepper, not one can.
Use 1 tsp freshly squeezed juice; reserve the rest for another use.

ingredients: 4 fully cooked, bun-length all-beef hot dogs, about 3 oz each; natural casing preferred, or skinless
2 oz sharp cheddar, cut into 4 thin slices
2 tablespoons unsalted butter, divided; soften 1 tablespoon for the buns
2 teaspoons avocado oil or another neutral high-heat oil, divided
1 medium yellow onion, about 6 to 8 oz, halved and thinly sliced crosswise
1/8 teaspoon kosher salt, for the onions
1/4 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper, for the onions
3 tablespoons drained pickled jalapenos, chopped into small pieces
3 tablespoons drained dill pickles, chopped into small pieces
1 small chipotle pepper in adobo, finely minced (about 2 teaspoons), plus 1 teaspoon adobo sauce from the same can
Water, as needed for reheating the franks and loosening the onions
instructions: Prepare the toppings: Stir together the mayonnaise, Dijon mustard, minced chipotle, adobo sauce, lime juice, and garlic powder in a small bowl. For gentler heat, start with half the chipotle and add the rest to taste. In a second bowl, combine the chopped pickled jalapenos and dill pickles. Blot them before mixing if they are wet; the relish should be crunchy, not sitting in brine. Refrigerate both bowls while cooking.

Brown the onions: Heat 1 tablespoon butter and 1 teaspoon oil in the skillet over medium heat. Add the sliced onion, salt, and black pepper. Cook for 15 to 20 minutes, stirring every couple of minutes, until soft with plenty of golden-brown edges. Reduce the heat if the edges darken before the centers soften. Add a tablespoon of water at a time to release browned bits when necessary, letting it evaporate before continuing. These are golden sauteed onions, not fully caramelized onion jam.

Finish the onions: Stir in the Worcestershire sauce and cook for 30 to 60 seconds, until the onions are glossy and no watery liquid remains. Transfer to a plate and keep warm. Do not add more salt yet; the franks, cheese, and pickles bring their own seasoning.

Gently heat the franks: While the onions cook, bring enough water to cover the franks to a gentle simmer in a wide saucepan, then reduce the heat so the water is barely moving. Add the franks and heat until steaming hot throughout, generally 8 to 12 minutes depending on thickness; use 165 F / 74 C at the center as this recipe's reheating target. Follow any more stringent package instruction. Do not boil hard. Keep natural casings intact rather than slashing or spiral-cutting them. Coordinate the timing so the buns are ready when the franks are hot.

Toast the buns: Wipe any scorched onion residue from the skillet and return it to medium heat. Open the buns without breaking their hinges and spread the remaining 1 tablespoon softened butter thinly over the cut faces. Toast cut-side down for 1 to 2 minutes, working in batches as needed, until golden and crisp at the surface while the buns remain soft inside. Set them cut-side up, uncovered, so the toasted faces do not steam.

Sear the franks: Lift the heated franks from the water and pat them thoroughly dry. Add the remaining 1 teaspoon oil to the skillet and heat over medium-high until shimmering but not smoking. Add the franks and brown for about 2 to 3 minutes total, turning with tongs to develop several browned patches. Stop before the casings split; lower the heat if they puff aggressively. The centers are already hot, so this is a brief browning step, not a long cook.

Soften the cheese: Reduce the skillet heat to low. Fold or trim each thin cheddar slice lengthwise to sit over one frank rather than spread across the pan. Cover for 30 to 60 seconds, just until the cheese softens and begins to melt, then remove the franks promptly. Do not add water for this step.

Assemble and serve: Spread about 1 tablespoon chipotle mayo inside each toasted bun. Add a cheese-topped frank, about 2 tablespoons golden onions, and 1 to 1 1/2 tablespoons well-drained jalapeno-pickle relish. Serve immediately, with extra toppings alongside rather than loading them all onto the buns. Each bite should still taste primarily of the beef frank.
notes: Original recipe developed for this collection; not kitchen-tested. Times are estimates, so prioritize visual and temperature cues. No star rating or nutrition estimate is claimed.
Use purchased, fully cooked all-beef franks. This is not a recipe for grinding, curing, emulsifying, or stuffing homemade sausages. Start with a frank whose flavor you enjoy on its own.
Natural casings provide the intended snap. Skinless franks can use the same method, but the bite will be different. Do not compensate with a long, drying sear.

For milder heat, use half the chipotle and replace half the pickled jalapenos with more dill pickle. For more heat, add another small chipotle to the mayo and replace some dill pickle with hot pickled jalapenos. Keep the total relish quantity similar so the bun is not overloaded. Pepper heat varies by brand.

Drain the relish, cook off excess onion liquid, dry the franks before searing, and leave toasted bun faces uncovered. Use soft buns sized to the franks and thin slices of regular sharp cheddar rather than thick pieces of very aged cheese. Bacon and cheese sauce are not needed for the base version.

For a grill finish, gently heat the franks as directed, pat dry, then brown briefly over direct medium-high heat, turning frequently. Move off direct heat to soften the cheese and toast the buttered buns separately. Stop before natural casings burst.

The mayo, drained relish, and cooked onions can be prepared one day ahead and refrigerated separately at 40 F / 4 C or colder. Reheat onions until steaming hot and evaporate excess moisture. Toast buns, finish franks, and assemble immediately before eating. Refrigerate perishable leftovers within 2 hours, or within 1 hour above 90 F / 32 C.

The structured grocery list covers the base recipe's purchased ingredients. Water is excluded. One lime supplies the measured teaspoon of juice; the chipotle pepper and adobo sauce come from the same can. Optional heat adjustments are not included in base shopping quantities.

Technique reference: Daniel Gritzer and Joshua Bousel, The Best Grilled Hot Dogs, Serious Eats, https://www.seriouseats.com/best-grilled-hot-dogs-recipe . The gentle-heat-then-sear principle informed this original stovetop adaptation; the topping formula and wording are original, not their tested dish.
Food-safety reference: USDA FSIS, Hot Dogs and Food Safety, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/meat-catfish/hot-dogs-food-safety .
